reader.requirement: At 85 a relative-file statement that meets a permanent error (30; 35 OPEN INPUT/I-O/EXTEND of an absent non-optional file; 37 open mode unsupported; 38 file previously closed with lock; 39 fixed-attribute conflict) is unsuccessful with a 3x status, runs any applicable exception procedure, and the condition stays in effect for later operations on the file until an implementor-defined technique corrects it.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector (from 2002): at 85 the PHYSICAL FILE is marked closed with lock
the same behaviour: at 85 every OPEN of that physical file through any file-name answers 38; from 2002 only the locking connector

DialectBehavior.RelativeWriteKeyOutOfRangeIsPermanentError (from 2014): a random or dynamic WRITE whose key is below 1 or above the highest RRN answers the invalid key 24 at 85, the permanent error 34 at 2014 and 2023
ctx.Data.DialectLevel >= 2002 picks the void __RunUse body with the GR17 SORT exit filter; at 85 the plain void body. It decides how the procedure is invoked, not whether it is selected

DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility (from 2002): off at 85, so no 5x/6x sharing status can replace a 1985 value; a second OPEN of an open physical file through another file-name is not a sharing conflict

reader.notes: The Status setter records any 3x status on an open connector and every verb but CLOSE replays it first (PermanentErrorReplay), so the persistence sentence holds at 85; probe p6torn witnesses it with a real 30, which the witness case said it could not raise. A directory answers 35 on OPEN INPUT and 37 on OPEN OUTPUT; both are 3x, and the value is the implementor's choice. The status class tests (CodeGen/Verbs/IoStatusClass.cs), the generated __IoCheck hook (DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery) and the Status setter's permanent-error record are the same code at every edition.

refuter.evidence: runs/r4a-001 at --std 85: a SEQUENTIAL file opened INPUT and I-O as RELATIVE -> 39 (USE runs), READ after it 47, CLOSE 42; a 4-byte relative file opened with an 8-byte FD -> 39 (§1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR8 lets the implementor validate it); OPEN I-O of absent non-optional dynamic file -> 35, WRITE 48, OPEN OUTPUT 00 then WRITE 00; CLOSE WITH LOCK then OPEN INPUT 38 and OPEN I-O 38 again (§1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR5 'without the LOCK phrase'). Persistence after a failed OPEN reads as the documented technique (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-105: a failed OPEN leaves the connector closed, CLOSE ends the condition), and '48' after a '35' is covered by 'If more than one value applies, the implementor determines which'. cite.py: 'OK §1985:VIII.1.3.4 GR4 (1.3.4 I-O Status) the text is in GR4'; 'OK §1985:VIII.1.3.4 GRL2.4'; 'OK §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR5 (4.4.4 General Rules)'.
